contract.proves:
The controller's reconcile loop must actually converge, not merely run.

WHY THIS EXISTS

On 2026-07-31 the cluster reported healthy by every existing probe — five
nodes heartbeating, services registered, etcd quorate — while the reconcile
loop failed on every single pass and converged nothing. `cluster.health`
said "healthy" the whole time. Nothing in the suite contradicted it, so a
48-minute run produced 18 failures whose shared root cause was invisible.

A liveness signal is not a convergence signal. This scenario asserts the
difference.

WHAT IT CATCHES

  - workflow definition "cluster.reconcile" not found
    (Day-0 did not deploy /var/lib/globular/workflows — the whole 2026-07-31
    cascade started here)
  - reconcile circuit breaker stuck OPEN
  - intent resolution failed: unknown profile: "ai"
    (cluster_controller/handlers_status.go derives profiles["ai"] from
    installed AI packages, but component_catalog/profilemap.go defines only
    compute/control-plane/core/database/dns/gateway/media-server/scylla/
    storage — so the node's intent never resolves)
  - INVARIANT VIOLATION: MinioPoolNodes[N] is not a valid IP
    (join flow writing hostnames where the contract requires IPs)

WHAT IT DELIBERATELY IGNORES

"handled by release pipeline workflow" and "materialize-infra: skipping …"
are normal delegation, not errors.

NOTE ON TIMING: bootstrap legitimately logs transient reconcile failures
while services are still coming up. The settle wait below exists so this
measures steady state, not Day-0 noise.
